newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No C&W approach yet on Optus-Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: No C&W approach yet on Optus-Australia govt.

text.p: Australian communications mininster Richard Alston said on Friday the government had not yet been approached by Cable and Wireless Plc about the British firm lifting its stake in Optus Communications Pty Ltd.
But a government source said it was understood that Cable and Wireless intends to approach the government to lift its stake in Australia's second largest telecommunications carrier.
"We are not privy to negotiation between the two main stakeholders," Alston told reporters, adding that the Optus board was meeting on Friday and there may be some development following the meeting.
"If there is any desire on the part of Cable and Wireless or even BellSouth to increase their holding they need to seek approval and they haven't sought that yet," Alston said.
Cable and Wireless (C&W) has been tipped to double its stake in Optus to 49 percent soon through the buy-out of BellSouth Corp Inc 24.5 percent stake.

The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Friday that C&W officials had spoken to the government about a possible shareholding change and a relaxation of rules limiting foreign shareholders to 49 percent ownership of Optus.
The major Optus shareholder is Australian transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless Ltd, which had hoped to sell its stake in later this year in conjunction with a float.

Earlier this month, Optus appointed former C&W executive Peter Howell-Davies as its chief executive officer, replacing Ziggy Switkowski, who resigned after a year of rising losses at Optus' pay television operations.
These losses and the management change has forced the indefinite postponement of the float.
